source.check: page image read (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9): 'Glenlark—Mr. Solomon Morris in place of Mr. Daniel M'Crea' among 'the only changes on the Council'; block image read (Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5, section 2.91) prints the change as Solomon Morris (N.) for Daniel M'Crea; the member sat at the new council's first meeting (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5)

note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors. Nominations were received on Tuesday 5 May 1936 and there was no contest in any division: the Unionists nominated for the 21 divisions in which they held majorities and the Nationalists for ten, and the retiring members for the divisions without a nomination were deemed re-elected (Mid-Ulster Mail, 9 May 1936, p. 9; Ulster Herald, 9 May 1936, p. 5). Polling in County Tyrone was fixed for Wednesday 3 June 1936; no poll was needed. The new council first met on Monday 8 June 1936 (Ulster Herald, 13 June 1936, p. 5). Solomon Morris was returned unopposed for Glenlark in place of Daniel M'Crea, one of the changes printed with the division. Returned unopposed.
